items.name: RayInterval
items.signature: pub struct RayInterval

docs.body:
Intersect a normalized ray with a finite sphere and clamp the result to
 `[0, max_distance]`. All inputs are finite and `radius`/`max_distance` are
 non-negative domain parameters. This clips a rendering/search DOMAIN; it
 says nothing about whether an implicit surface exists inside that domain.
 Callers can consequently avoid marching known-empty space without
 replacing their field evaluator with an analytic surface intersection.

The same finite-sphere interval specialized for a camera whose origin is
 `target - unit_forward * camera_distance`. Forward-facing camera rays and
 the caller's finite distance/radius bounds guarantee intersections lie in
 front of the camera. This avoids reconstructing the target offset in every
 fragment while preserving the general interval above for arbitrary rays.

docs.body:
A continuous sample position inside the integer pixel `(px, py)`.

 `ordered_2x2` places one sample in each quarter of every 2x2 pixel block.
 The four offsets average to the pixel centre, but no sample sits on the
 centre-aligned lattice that makes thin, rotated boundaries stair-step in
 lockstep. It is deliberately ONE sample per pixel: expensive implicit
 surfaces and deep fractals gain spatially stratified refinement without
 multiplying their dominant orbit/ray-march loop. The construction is
 branch-free and contains no renderer-specific quality or LoD policy.

 responsive surfaces neither crop a low-resolution square nor stretch a
 non-square viewport. Browser code supplies only the measured extent;
 this Fe construction owns the projection policy.

```fe
pub fn targeted_camera_sphere_interval(
    _ unit_forward: Vec3,
    _ unit_direction: Vec3,
    _ camera_distance: f32,
    _ radius: f32,
) -> RayInterval
```

 The same finite-sphere interval specialized for a camera whose origin is
 `target - unit_forward * camera_distance`. Forward-facing camera rays and
 the caller's finite distance/radius bounds guarantee intersections lie in
 front of the camera. This avoids reconstructing the target offset in every
 fragment while preserving the general interval above for arbitrary rays.

```fe
pub fn unit_ray_sphere_interval(
    _ origin: Vec3,
    _ unit_direction: Vec3,
    _ center: Vec3,
    _ radius: f32,
    _ max_distance: f32,
) -> RayInterval
```

 Intersect a normalized ray with a finite sphere and clamp the result to
 `[0, max_distance]`. All inputs are finite and `radius`/`max_distance` are
 non-negative domain parameters. This clips a rendering/search DOMAIN; it
 says nothing about whether an implicit surface exists inside that domain.
 Callers can consequently avoid marching known-empty space without
 replacing their field evaluator with an analytic surface intersection.
